newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin raps top prosecutor over unsolved crimes.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin raps top prosecutor over unsolved crimes.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin told Russia's chief prosecutor on Tuesday he was dissatisfied with his work and warned him that public anger was rising over his failure to solve a growing list of murders.

"Behind the overall figures, which I am well acquainted with, are hidden some prominent murders which the whole of society is seething about," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as telling Prosecutor-General Yuri Skuratov at the Kremlin.
Interfax said Yeltsin had told him "in sharp terms" that he was unhappy with his work and he must put the prosecutor-general's office in order.
Crime, much of it involving mafia-style gangs, has risen sharply since the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.

Many murders go unsolved and Skuratov has been ridiculed for failing to solve prominent cases such as the blowing up of newspaper reporter Dmitry Kholodov and the shooting of television journalist Vladislav Listyev two years ago.
"Despite your repeated assertions that the Listyev case is nearing an end, this and other cases are practically buried. This is impermissible," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as saying.
